items.title: Minuut-secrete missive, geschreven op last van de Raad aan de raad van Indie, C.J. Prediger te Batavia, door de secretaris van de raad, Mr. J.C. Smissaert, bijgevoegde overbrenging in cijfer en minuut-post-scriptum (van latere datum) toegevoegd aan een op 20 april 1801 verzonden triplicaat dezer missive

files.209_leaf1.jpg: order 1 -- dispatch-record cover memo (Origineel/Duplicaat/Triplicaat routing note), plain Dutch, no cipher
files.209_leaf2.jpg: order 2 -- bifolium; left page is the tail of an unrelated earlier plain-Dutch draft; right page opens '20 Nov. 1800 / van Prediger / Geacht vriend!' in plain, then the cipher body (paired-digit-row cipher, see zoom)
files.209_leaf2_cipher_zoom.jpg: native-res crop of the cipher opening on leaf 2's right page -- two aligned rows of numerals: a longer top row of multi-digit cipher groups, a shorter single-digit row directly beneath most/every digit of the top row
files.209_leaf3.jpg: order 3 -- bifolium, both pages very faint/low-contrast, apparently mirror-image ink bleed-through from the facing recto rather than the recto's own ink; the same paired-digit-row cipher pattern is visible but hard to read
files.209_leaf3_zoom.jpg: native-res crop of leaf 3's faint cipher rows
files.209_leaf4.jpg: order 4 -- reverts to plain Dutch: continues and closes the letter body, signed '(getekend) Smissaert', dated 'Amsterdam den 20 November 1800', with a same-day P.S. about Council membership (Mr. Daniel van Laer's appointment) -- all plain, no cipher
files.209_leaf5.jpg: order 5 -- a separate, later postscript entirely in plain Dutch, dated 'Amst. 20 April 1801', signed '(getekend) Smissaert' -- matches the unittitle's 'minuut-post-scriptum (van latere datum)'

items.title: Stukken over het aan Elout en Van Grasveld medegegeven cijfer

files.317_leaf1_alphabet.jpg: order 1 -- 'Alphabeth tot een Cijferschrift, om het welk te schrijven en te ontcyfferen, men een gegeven woord of slegte klanken zonder betekenis nodig heeft': a 13-row reciprocal/tabula-recta-style alphabet table (rows headed Z.Y, X.W, V.U, T.S, R.Q, P.O, N.M, L.K, J.I, H.G, F.E, D.C, B.A), each row a full a-z substitution alphabet, with a note that the system can be arranged 'op 200 veel verschillende manieren' as long as sender and recipient share the same table
files.317_leaf2_example.jpg: order 2 -- 'Voorbeeld': a fully worked example keying the table with the word 'Nebawo' (repeated over the plaintext 'de zaak zal geld kosten') and giving the resulting ciphertext letter by letter -- a complete worked demonstration of the cipher method, not an actual secret dispatch
files.317_leaf3_blank_verso.jpg: order 3 -- blank versos, faint bleed-through only
